items.summary: EntityType is a named type, not a raw string — mocks must match the exact return type
items.details: core.EntityType is defined as 'type EntityType string' — a distinct named type. A mock that returns string instead of EntityType compiles if the mock does not claim to satisfy an interface, but fails when assigned to core.Entity. The items/validation test failure (issue #612) is the canonical example. Always check: if an interface method returns a named type, your mock must return that exact named type.

items.summary: Never commit replace directives — they are dev-only conveniences that break CI
items.details: Local replace directives (replace github.com/foo => ../foo) resolve against local filesystem paths. CI does not have those paths. Even when CI checks out the full repo, go mod tidy produces a diff from the replace directives, which CI can treat as a failure. The CLAUDE.md rule is unambiguous: NEVER add replace directives. Remove them before committing. The four modules in issue #613 are the result of development shortcuts that became permanent.

items.summary: Bulk error collection in Remove() — PR #603
items.details: BusEffect.Remove() must unsubscribe all active handlers, not stop at the first failure. PR #603 fixed Condition.Remove() to collect all unsubscribe errors. The pattern: var errs []error; for each ID, if unsubscribe fails append to errs; set subscriptions nil; return errors.Join(errs...). Stopping at first failure leaves orphaned subscriptions that fire on events after removal.

items.summary: make pre-commit only covers core + events — not the full repo
items.details: The Makefile pre-commit target runs fmt, tidy, lint, and tests for core and events only. Before committing changes to mechanics/*, tools/*, rulebooks/*, items run per-module go test ./... and golangci-lint run ./... manually. make test-all covers all modules but currently fails at items/ (issue #612).

items.summary: rulebooks/dnd5e/dungeon has correct dependency direction but wrong layer location
items.details: dungeon/ imports tools/environments and tools/spatial (lower layers — correct). The problem is not a dependency inversion but the module location: dungeon logic belongs at the Tools layer so rpg-api can import dungeon generation without importing the full dnd5e rulebook. The planned move is architectural relocation, not a dependency fix.

items.summary: Toolkit ADR and journey docs are load-bearing context, not archive material — do not apply platform-mcp doc shape mechanically
items.details: The previous invocation bootstrapped docs by adding copies of docs/adr/ and docs/journey/ into docs/archive/, treating them as legacy. Kirk corrected: the ADRs and journey docs record how the engine came to be and are top-level docs, not archive material. The originals were never moved (they stayed at docs/adr/ and docs/journey/ all along); the archive copies were pure duplication added by the bootstrap commit. Fix: git rm the 116 archive copies. Rule going forward: ADRs stay forever (superseded ones get a note, not deletion); journey docs stay as exploration history. The platform-mcp doc shape is a starting point, not a constraint — toolkit is foundational in a way other repos aren't. When in doubt, the toolkit's own history matters more than structural uniformity.

items.summary: Plans judgment call: toolkit docs/plans/ is top-level; the single legitimately-archived plan stays in docs/archive/plans/
items.details: docs/plans/ contains 10 feature design plans (Dec 2025-Jan 2026). These are toolkit-specific exploration — some implemented, some stale — and they live at top-level because they document the toolkit's design history. A single older plan (2025-12-06-ac-system-design.md) was legitimately moved into docs/archive/plans/ by commit 3dd2b98 (Dec 2025) before the ideas/plans distinction was clear; it has no duplicate in docs/plans/ and was left in place. The 10 copies added by the bootstrap commit were removed.

items.summary: Ideas judgment call: toolkit docs/ideas/ is top-level; it is toolkit-specific design memory, not rpg-project/ideas/ territory
items.details: docs/ideas/ has 3 idea directories (action-economy-history, monster-behavior, type-safe-refs). These are toolkit-scoped design explorations that predate the rpg-project/ideas/ convention. rpg-project/ideas/ owns cross-repo ideas; toolkit/docs/ideas/ owns toolkit-internal design history. They are not duplicates. The archive copies were removed; the originals stay at top-level.
